events.title: The Abbasids defeat the Umayyads at the Battle of the Zab
events.description: Abbasid rebels defeated the army of the Umayyad Caliphate on the banks of the Great Zab, in present-day Iraq. The battle spelled the end of the Umayyad Caliphate and the rise of the Abbasids, who ruled as caliphs until 1258.

events.title: Edward III is proclaimed king of England in London
events.description: After Queen Isabella and Roger Mortimer invaded England and summoned a parliament, King Edward II was forced to give up the throne, and his fourteen-year-old son was proclaimed king in London. He was crowned at Westminster Abbey on 1 February.

events.title: An earthquake centred in Friuli is felt across Europe
events.description: An earthquake centred in the South Alpine region of Friuli was felt across Europe; according to contemporary sources churches and houses collapsed and villages were destroyed. It struck in the same year that the Great Plague ravaged Italy.

events.title: Henry VIII secretly marries Anne Boleyn
events.description: Henry married the pregnant Anne Boleyn in a private ceremony at Whitehall while still married to Catherine of Aragon. To make the marriage lawful he broke with Rome and headed his own Church of England.

events.title: Jesuit missionaries found São Paulo
events.description: Manuel da Nóbrega and José de Anchieta celebrated Mass at a new Jesuit mission on the Piratininga plateau. The settlement grew into São Paulo, now the largest city in the Southern Hemisphere.
events.html: Manuel da Nóbrega and José de Anchieta celebrated Mass at a new Jesuit mission on the Piratininga plateau. The settlement grew into São Paulo, now the largest city in the Southern Hemisphere.

events.title: Takeda Shingen crushes Tokugawa Ieyasu at Mikatagahara
events.description: On the plain of Mikatagahara north of Hamamatsu, Takeda Shingen's army encircled the Tokugawa-Oda force and almost totally annihilated it; many of Ieyasu's retainers were killed. Shingen was seeking a route to Kyoto in his campaign against Oda Nobunaga.

events.title: Queen Victoria's eldest daughter marries Prince Frederick of Prussia
events.description: Victoria, the Princess Royal, married the future German Emperor Frederick III at St James's Palace. Mendelssohn's 'Wedding March' played as they left, starting a fashion for it at weddings.

events.title: Edison and Bell interests form the Oriental Telephone Company
events.description: Companies holding the telephone patents of Thomas Edison and Alexander Graham Bell combined to form the Oriental Telephone Company. It built early telephone exchanges in India and other parts of Asia.

events.title: First Winter Olympics open at Chamonix
events.description: An 'International Winter Sports Week' opened at Chamonix in the French Alps with athletes from 16 nations. The International Olympic Committee later recognised it as the first Winter Olympic Games.
events.html: An 'International Winter Sports Week' opened at Chamonix in the French Alps with athletes from 16 nations. The International Olympic Committee later recognised it as the first Winter Olympic Games.

events.title: Battle of the Bulge ends in Allied victory
events.description: Allied forces restored their line in the Ardennes, ending Germany's last major offensive in the west. Fought in bitter winter conditions, it was the costliest American battle of the Second World War.

events.title: Idi Amin seizes power in Uganda
events.description: While President Milton Obote was abroad, army commander Idi Amin took power in a coup. His eight-year rule saw the expulsion of Uganda's Asians and the killing of an estimated 100,000 to 500,000 people.
